[spoiler=[b]The Great Jihad - Part 1[/b]
[i]In the desolation of ambition, the cost of loyalty is often measured in blood[/i]]
The harsh midday sun of west shamat shined down on the first unit of Sal-Baliz fighters, on their way to liberate Mecca. Instead of their usual black attire, they instead wore white robes and sand coloured military uniform, in order to blend into their bleak surroundings. Although they are not yet aware that the supreme leaders communication was compromised, they still know that they cannot take any risks. If even a bird flies overhead they are to drop down to the ground and cover their heads, in the hope that they wont be spotted. Food and water is scarce in the Sal-Baliz, so not much was provided for the unit. They are all experiencing the symptoms of dehydration, but no one shows it, they are too afraid of the commander, Abd-El-Kader bin Tamir, or Abd for short. Even the way the commander walks instills fear in those who meet him.

Suddenly, one of the junior soldiers fell to the ground.
Get up! Abd shouted at him. He repeated himself twice, before kicking the young man.
Water I need water, he groaned, his mouth half filled with sand. One of the other younger members of the unit reached for his water rations and began to offer it to the other.
How disappointing said Abd as he reached for his rifle.
wait! Stop! Dont kill him-
*BANG, BANG*
The sound of gunshots pierced through the air and echoed across the endless desert as the two bodies lay lifeless in the sand. They would remain their as a reminder of the cruelty of the Sal-Baliz[/spoiler]
